Total 7 models

Fireworks offers 7 models, each with different intelligence, performance, and pricing characteristics. Below is a comparison of the key metrics across models.

  • For intelligence, the top models on Fireworks are Kimi K3 (max) (44), Kimi K3 (max) (FAST) (44), and GLM-5.3-Flash (42).
  • For output speed, the fastest models are Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) (417 t/s), GLM-5.3-Flash (188 t/s), and MiniMax-M3 (183 t/s). Speed varies significantly across models, with a 232% difference between the fastest and slowest.
  • For latency, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) (5.37s), MiniMax-M3 (11.77s), and GLM-5.3-Flash (12.04s) offer the lowest time to first answer token.
  • For pricing, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) ($0.04), GLM-5.3-Flash ($0.10), and MiniMax-M3 ($0.22) offer the lowest blended prices per 1M tokens. Prices vary up to 31.8x across models.
  • For context window size, Kimi K3 (max) (1M), Kimi K3 (max) (FAST) (1M), and GLM-5.3-Flash (1M) support the largest context windows on Fireworks.
  • Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) offers both the fastest output and best pricing, making it attractive for throughput-sensitive and cost-conscious applications. Kimi K3 (max) leads in intelligence for tasks that require the highest quality.

Speed

Measured by Output Speed (tokens per second)

Output Speed

Output tokens per second · Higher is better

Tokens per second received while the model is generating tokens (ie. after first chunk has been received from the API for models which support streaming).

Figures represent performance of the model's first-party API or the median across providers where a first-party API is not available.

Latency

Measured by Time (seconds) to First Token

Latency: Time To First Answer Token

Seconds to first answer token received · Accounts for reasoning model 'thinking' time

Time to first answer token received, in seconds, after API request sent. For reasoning models, this includes the 'thinking' time of the model before providing an answer. For models which do not support streaming, this represents time to receive the completion.

Cache Behaviour

Cache Hit Rate

Share of cacheable input tokens served from cache · Median of the last four weeks, updated Sep 26, 2026

The share of cacheable input tokens served from the provider's prompt cache, measured during multi-turn agentic coding sessions. We regularly measure each endpoint and report a representative rate based on recent measurements. Higher values mean more of the input is billed at the cheaper cache-hit price, where the provider offers one, which lowers the effective cost of agentic workloads. For further details, see our methodology page.

Cost per Task vs. Cache Hit Rate

Weighted average cost (USD) per Intelligence Index task · Cache hit rate: median of the last four weeks, updated Sep 26, 2026
Most attractive quadrant
Pareto line

Weighted average cost per Intelligence Index task. Each evaluation’s cost is calculated from input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices, divided by task count, and weighted by its Intelligence Index weight.

Frequently Asked Questions

Common questions about Fireworks

Fireworks offers 7 models that we track: Kimi K3 (max), Kimi K3 (max) (FAST), GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, MiniMax-M3, Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16).

The most intelligent model available on Fireworks is Kimi K3 (max) with an Intelligence Index score of 44.

The fastest model on Fireworks by output speed is Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) at 417.2 tokens per second.

The model with the lowest time to first answer token on Fireworks is Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) at 5.37s. Lower latency means faster initial response time.

The most affordable model on Fireworks by blended price is Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) at $0.04 per 1M tokens (7:2:1 cache hit/input/output ratio).

Prices on Fireworks vary up to 94x across models, from $0.04 per 1M tokens for Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16) to $3.46 per 1M tokens for Kimi K3 (max) (FAST).

Yes, Fireworks offers an OpenAI-compatible API, making it easy to switch from OpenAI or use existing OpenAI SDK integrations.

Yes, all 7 models on Fireworks support JSON mode for structured output.

Yes, all 7 models on Fireworks support function calling (tool use).

Yes, Fireworks offers 7 reasoning models: Kimi K3 (max), Kimi K3 (max) (FAST), GLM-5.3-Flash, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, MiniMax-M3, Nemotron 3 Ultra, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (BF16). Reasoning models use extended thinking to work through complex problems before providing an answer.

Yes, all 7 models on Fireworks are open weight models.

Yes, provider performance can vary over time due to infrastructure changes, load balancing, and updates. We continuously benchmark all providers and display historical performance trends in the "Over Time" charts.

When choosing a model on Fireworks, consider: intelligence (for quality-sensitive tasks), output speed (for throughput-intensive tasks), latency (for interactive applications requiring quick first responses), pricing (for cost-sensitive workloads), and features like context window size, JSON mode, or function calling support.
